Evan: Quick summary of the hedged coalesce sweep I ran on bench-cluster-3 — asking for eyeballs before I schedule a larger run.
Evan: Setup: 13k-token synthetic mixture, steady QPS ~1200, models: redwood-open-13b / quant-int8 variants. Baseline (no hedging): coalesce_delay_ms=4, jitter_max_ms=3.
Evan: Sweep targets: reduce coalesce_delay, add per-request randomized hedging, and cap token budget per microbatch to reduce KV churn.
Evan: Key observation: when coalesce_delay_ms <= 2 with jitter_max_ms <=1 we see 99.9p latency regressions (+18–45ms) vs baseline. Kernel-selector logs show frequent kernel fallback and increased memcpy time.
Evan: KV cache stats corroborate: kv_miss_rate jumped 4% -> ~18% and evictions/sec spiked. Hypothesis: overly aggressive coalescing with tiny jitter causes many slightly overlapping batches that evict hot KV entries before reuse.
Evan: Experiment config I used (small snippet):
Evan: ```
Evan: hedged_coalesce: true
Evan: coalesce_delay_ms: [1,2,4]
Evan: jitter_max_ms: [0,1,5]
Evan: token_budget_per_microbatch: 1024
Evan: hedging_timeout_ms: 6   # if request waits > this, send hedged microbatch
Evan: batch_size_cap: 8
Evan: ```
Alex: Nice writeup. Two quick Qs: can you paste the kernel-selector trace and the KV eviction timeline? also which CPU/GPU instance? 
Evan: Kernel trace: lots of rapid kernel-switch events, sample line: `kernel_select: prefer_gemm=false -> fallback_int8 @ t=0.002s` . GPU flavor: A10G; host mem pressure modest but GPU l2 thrash visible.
Evan: KV eviction timeline: evictions align tightly with microbatch dispatch spikes. When coalesce_delay is 1ms we get ~3x eviction bursts vs 4ms.
Maria: Thought: try hedged_coalesce but with a small *positive* jitter window (e.g., uniform 1–4ms) instead of [0,1]. That spreads arrivals, reduces synchronized evictions. Also consider token_budget soft-limit with leaky refill so a single long sequence doesn't flush cache.
Rhea: Also try forcing kernel binding for the short sequence path: `kernel_binding: prefer_gemm=true` in the canary. If kernel switching causes copy overhead that's adding latency.
Alex: Can we also try microbatch interval alignment with KV keepalive? e.g., extend KV TTL by 50ms for primed keys to tolerate small inter-batch gaps.
Evan: I ran a quick 6k-sample A/B: config A (coalesce_delay=1, jitter=0, budget=1024) vs B (coalesce_delay=2, jitter in [1,4], budget=1024, hedging_timeout=6). Results: median latencies close, but B 99.9p is 22ms lower. KV miss_rate in A: 17.9%, in B: 6.1%.
Evan: CPU/GPU profiler snippets show B has fewer memcpy peaks and less context switching in kernel-selector.
Maria: Nice. Sounds like the combination of tiny jitter=0 + tiny delay is the worst case (synchrony). Hedging + randomized jitter breaks that.
Rhea: Request: can you run two more variants before we change defaults: (1) same as B but token_budget_per_microbatch=2048, (2) same as B but hedging_timeout_ms=3. I want to see tradeoffs on throughput vs 99.9p.
InfraBot: deploy-canary job queued: job_id=deploy-hedged-sweep-1976543210. Running fixture set against bench-cluster-3.
Evan: Will run those two variants + kernel_binding=prefer_gemm toggles. I'll attach perf graphs and a short runbook for ops if this lands in default runtime.
Evan: Ops runbook draft note: if 99.9p increases after change, rollback toggle is `runtime.coalesce.hedged=false` and `runtime.coalesce.coalesce_delay_ms=4` — keep an eye on kv.evictions/s and kernel_select_fallbacks per pod.
Alex: thx — ping us when the new graphs are available. :thumbsup:
Maria: minor: add a metric for microbatch_overlap_ratio so we can detect this synchrony automatically.
Evan: Good call, I'll add it to the next sweep. Thanks everyone.
